name: CLEVR: Compositional Language and Elementary Visual Reasoning
description: CLEVR is a diagnostic visual reasoning dataset created by Stanford University and Facebook AI Research to isolate and evaluate compositional visual question answering. It contains 100,000 synthetic 3D rendered scenes and approximately 1,000,000 automatically generated questions testing visual reasoning abilities: counting, spatial relationship comparison, logical operations (AND, OR, NOT), and attribute identification (shape, color, material, size).

citation.paper_title: CLEVR: A Diagnostic Dataset for Compositional Language and Elementary Visual Reasoning

provenance.collection_method: Synthetic 3D scenes rendered using Blender with random object configurations; questions generated from functional programs over scene ground-truth graphs.
provenance.curation_notes: Engineered specifically to minimize statistical question bias and avoid shortcuts prevalent in human-collected VQA datasets.
